rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quṭb says humans deny their Lord’s favors and generous beneficence; this ingratitude appears in varied words and deeds.
rows.anchor: إن الإنسان ليجحد نعمة ربه ، وينكر جزيل فضله . ويتمثل كنوده وجحوده في مظاهر شتى تبدو منه أفعالا وأقوالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quṭb leaves the pleasant life undescribed in detail so its shade of contentment is felt; this is the most restful bliss.
rows.anchor: ويدعها مجملة بلا تفصيل ، توقع في الحس ظلال الرضى وهو أروح النعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a child’s mother is its refuge, the people’s refuge and return on that Day is the Abyss; the elegant, partly obscure image prepares its later clarification and intensifies the effect.
rows.anchor: والأم هي مرجع الطفل وملاذه . فمرجع القوم وملاذهم يومئذ هو الهاوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quṭb discusses faith’s nature and value in life, not its juristic definition: it connects finite humanity to the eternal source, the cosmos, its laws, and its stored powers, widening human strength, lifespan, and horizon.
rows.anchor: نحن لا نعرف الإيمان هنا تعريفه الفقهي ؛ ولكننا نتحدث عن طبيعته وقيمته في الحياة . إنه اتصال هذا الكائن الإنساني الفاني الصغير المحدود بالأصل المطلق الأزلي الباقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This connection lets people enjoy existence, beauty, and fellow creatures, making life a joyful divine festival and a gain beyond comparison; losing faith is incomparable loss.
rows.anchor: فإنه يمنحه إلى جانب هذا كله متاعا بالوجود وما فيه من جمال ، ومن مخلوقات تتعاطف أرواحها مع روحه . فإذا الحياة رحلة في مهرجان إلهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship of one God frees people from servitude to others, establishes their equality, and yields genuine liberation because only one power and deity exists.
rows.anchor: التعبد لإله واحد ، يرفع الإنسان عن العبودية لسواه ، ويقيم في نفسه المساواة مع جميع العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God-centeredness makes God the source of human values, laws, and judgments, replacing caprice and self-interest with revealed law and justice and giving believers confidence to withstand other value systems.
rows.anchor: والربانية التي تحدد الجهة التي يتلقى منها الإنسان تصوراته وقيمه وموازينه واعتباراته وشرائعه وقوانينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A clear, unmediated distinction between Creator and creature joins transient humanity to lasting truth, bringing inner light, calm, confidence, and relief from fear, anxiety, and unjust arrogance.
rows.anchor: ووضوح الصلة بين الخالق والمخلوق ، وتبين مقام الألوهية ومقام العبودية على حقيقتهما الناصعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Steadfast adherence to God’s way makes goodness purposeful, sustained, and cooperative across a Muslim community and successive generations rather than sporadic or temporary.
rows.anchor: والاستقامة على المنهج الذي يريده الله . فلا يكون الخير فلتة عارضة ، ولا نزوة طارئة ، ولا حادثة منقطعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in human dignity before God raises self-respect and moral shame; Quṭb condemns Darwinian, Freudian, and Marxist insinuations that degradation is natural and therefore nothing to feel ashamed of.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا كانت إيحاءات الدارونية والفرويدية والماركسية هي أبشع ما تبتلى به الفطرة البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human dignity and awareness that God sees consciences directly purify feelings; a believer senses God’s gaze and therefore cleans the inner self.
rows.anchor: ونظافة المشاعر تجيء نتيجة مباشرة للشعور بكرامة الإنسان على الله . ثم برقابة الله على الضمائر واطلاعه على السرائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moral sensibility naturally follows belief in a just, merciful, forgiving, loving God who hates evil, loves good, and knows hidden thoughts.
rows.anchor: والحاسة الأخلاقية ثمرة طبيعية وحتمية للإيمان بإله عادل رحيم عفو كريم ودود حليم ، يكره الشر ويحب الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Free will under God’s comprehensive watch entails individual and collective responsibility toward good and all humanity; believers therefore act alertly, weigh consequences, and recognize their worth and duty in existence.
rows.anchor: وهناك التبعة المترتبة على حرية الإرادة وشمول الرقابة ، وما تثيره في حس المؤمن من يقظة وحساسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith redirects competition from worldly attractions to God’s better, lasting reward (83:26), easing anxiety about immediate results; trust that God never forgets good sustains lifelong work and resistance to evil.
rows.anchor: والارتفاع عن التكالب على أعراض الحياة الدنيا - وهو بعض إيحاءات الإيمان - واختيار ما عند الله ، وهو خير وأبقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is the root and axis of every good: detached deeds wither, while faith organizes action into a coherent, purposeful, cooperative way of life.
rows.anchor: إن الإيمان هو أصل الحياة الكبير ، الذي ينبثق منه كل فرع من فروع الخير ، وتتعلق به كل ثمرة من ثماره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an nullifies deeds disconnected from faith, likening disbelievers’ work to windblown ash (14:18) and a mirage (24:39), since faith supplies an enduring motive and a goal aligned with existence’s purpose.
rows.anchor: مثل الذين كفروا بربهم أعمالهم كرماد اشتدت به الريح في يوم عاصف . لا يقدرون مما كسبوا على شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith reflects sound human nature and harmony with the cosmos; rejection indicates a defect in the human receiver and loss, and even apparently good deeds then lack validity.
rows.anchor: إن الإيمان دليل على صحة الفطرة وسلامة التكوين الإنساني ، وتناسقه مع فطرة الكون كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer’s expansive, beautiful, happy world makes the worlds of unbelievers appear narrow, low, distorted, miserable, and lost.
rows.anchor: وإن عالم المؤمن من السعة والشمول والامتداد والارتفاع والجمال والسعادة بحيث تبدو إلى جانبه عوالم غير المؤمنين صغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous action is faith’s natural fruit: once faith settles in the heart it moves outward; inert faith is counterfeit or dead, like a flower that gives off no fragrance.
rows.anchor: ما أن تستقر في الضمير حتى تسعى بذاتها إلى تحقيق ذاتها في الخارج في صورة عمل صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islamic faith means movement, action, building, and cultivation directed toward God, not inward withdrawal or good intentions without outward action.
rows.anchor: إنه ليس انكماشا وسلبية وانزواء في مكنونات الضمير . وليس مجرد النوايا الطيبة التي لا تتمثل في حركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God’s method is continuous, purposeful movement within existence, faith guides humanity to realize that same clean, constructive movement.
rows.anchor: وهذا المنهج حركة دائمة متصلة في صميم الوجود . صادرة عن تدبير ، متجهة إلى غاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual exhortation to truth and patience depicts a distinct, unified Muslim community that recognizes its duty to uphold truth, justice, and good and to lead humanity toward faith and righteous action.
rows.anchor: أما التواصي بالحق والتواصي بالصبر فتبرز من خلالها صورة الأمة المسلمة - أو الجماعة المسلمة - ذات الكيان الخاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exhorting one another to truth is essential because desire, self-interest, social assumptions, tyrants, and injustice obstruct it; mutual encouragement multiplies effort and keeps a cooperative community guarding the truth.
rows.anchor: والتواصي بالحق ضرورة . فالنهوض بالحق عسير . والمعوقات عن الحق كثيرة : هوى النفس ، ومنطق المصلحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual exhortation to patience is essential for faith, good works, and defending justice amid self-struggle, opposition, suffering, brazen evil, and a long, slow path; shared purpose and support increase endurance.
rows.anchor: والتواصي بالصبر كذلك ضرورة . فالقيام على الإيمان والعمل الصالح ، وحراسة الحق والعدل ، من أعسر ما يواجه الفرد والجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quṭb laments humanity’s widespread worldly loss and especially Muslims’ abandonment of God’s method and the Islamic banner for ethnic flags, despite Islam’s having first given Arabs righteous leadership.
rows.anchor: هذا والمسلمون - أو أصحاب دعوى الإسلام بتعبير أدق - هم أبعد أهل الأرض عن هذا الخير

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
rows.claim: Al-Nadwi says Muslim leaders governed through revealed scripture and divine law rather than their own legislation, which he considers prone to ignorance, error, and injustice; he cites 6:122 and 5:8.
rows.anchor: أبو الحسن الندوي في كتابه القيم

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
rows.claim: Al-Nadwi says Muslim leaders received prolonged moral formation under Muhammad, avoided seeking office, and treated authority as a trust and divine test for which they would answer; he invokes a Prophetic warning and 28:83, 4:58, and 6:165.
rows.anchor: أبو الحسن الندوي في كتابه القيم

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
rows.claim: Al-Nadwi says Muslim rule served humanity rather than an Arab nation or empire, aiming to free people from servitude to people and bring them to God; he cites Rabīʿ b. ʿĀmir’s address to Yazdegerd.
rows.anchor: أبو الحسن الندوي في كتابه القيم

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
rows.claim: Al-Nadwi presents equality across peoples, with piety as the sole distinction (49:13); he recounts ʿUmar’s defense of an Egyptian struck by ʿAmr’s son and says Muslim rulers shared learning and government with all peoples.
rows.anchor: أبو الحسن الندوي في كتابه القيم

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
rows.claim: Al-Nadwi argues that human flourishing and sound civilization require balanced development of body, spirit, heart, mind, feeling, and action within a moral and religious social environment.
rows.anchor: أبو الحسن الندوي في كتابه القيم

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
rows.claim: Al-Nadwi presents the Rightly Guided Caliphate as history’s finest model: spiritual, ethical, religious, intellectual, and material strengths combined, with ethical government, prosperity, few crimes, and humane social relations.
rows.anchor: أبو الحسن الندوي في كتابه القيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quṭb says the rightly guided period embodied the civilization and banner of faith, good works, and communal exhortation outlined by Sūrat al-ʿAṣr.
rows.anchor: هذه بعض ملامح تلك الحقبة السعيدة التي عاشتها البشرية في ظل الدستور الإسلامي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earthly profit and loss pale beside the lasting afterlife outcome: Paradise and divine approval, or their loss; humans reach their appointed perfection or fall beneath even a stone in worth and comfort, as 78:40 depicts.
rows.anchor: في عالم الحقيقة ، هناك الربح والخسر : ربح الجنة والرضوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura sets one path out of loss: faith, righteous deeds, and a united community mutually guarding truth with patience; Quṭb reports that two Companions recited it to each other before parting as a mutual pledge.
rows.anchor: لم يتفرقا حتى يقرأ أحدهما على الآخر سورة  " العصر "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quṭb identifies Sūrat al-Humaza as Meccan, with nine verses.
rows.anchor: سورة الهمزة مكية وآياتها تسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura portrays a real pattern from the early mission that recurs everywhere: a mean, small-souled person lets wealth dominate and treats it as life’s highest value, believing it buys people’s dignity and honor.
rows.anchor: تعكس هذه السورة صورة من الصور الواقعية في حياة الدعوة في عهدها الأول . وهي في الوقت ذاته نموذج يتكرر في كل بيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealthy person imagines money can do anything, including warding off death, securing lasting life, and escaping God’s decree and judgment.
rows.anchor: كما يروح يحسب أن هذا المال إله قادر على كل شيء ؛ لا يعجز عن فعل شيء ! حتى دفع الموت وتخليد الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He obsessively counts and enjoys counting wealth, then grows arrogant and belittles people through verbal mockery, gestures, and contempt for their traits.
rows.anchor: ينطلق في هوس بهذا المال يعده ويستلذ تعداده ؛ وتنطلق في كيانه نفخة فاجرة ، تدفعه إلى الاستهانة بأقدار الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam abhors this faithless, ignoble character and forbids mockery and faultfinding elsewhere; Quṭb infers a real case of some polytheists targeting the Messenger and believers, but says reports naming individuals are unreliable.
rows.anchor: وقد وردت روايات بتعيين بعض الشخصيات . ولكنها ليست وثيقة . فنكتفي نحن بما قررناه عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning pairs the mocker’s offense with fitting punishment: the arrogant money-backed scoffer is discarded into the crushing Fire, whose divine attribution marks it as uniquely terrifying.
rows.anchor: المهمل المتردي في( الحطمة )التي تحطم كل ما يلقى إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire reaches the heart that bred mockery and arrogance; it encloses the victim without rescue or concern, binding him to a pillar like an unrespected beast.
rows.anchor: هذه النار مغلقة عليه ، لا ينقذه منها أحد ، ولا يسأل عنه فيها أحد ! وهو موثق فيها إلى عمود كما توثق البهائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harsh sound patterns and emphatic rhetorical devices intensify the threat: summary and obscurity, an awe-inspiring question, then explanation and amplification; the imagery and feeling match the mocker’s deed.
rows.anchor: وفي جرس الألفاظ تشديد : عدده . كلا . لينبذن . تطلع . ممددة وفي معاني العبارات توكيد بشتى أساليب التوكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an both follows and directs the mission; it is a decisive weapon that destroys opponents’ schemes, shakes enemies, and strengthens believers.
rows.anchor: لقد كان القرآن يتابع أحداث الدعوة ويقودها في الوقت ذاته . وكان هو السلاح البتار الصاعق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s response to the mocker condemns moral degradation and defends believers, assuring them God sees their humiliation, abhors it, and punishes it, thereby lifting their spirits above hostile schemes.
rows.anchor: وإنا لنرى في عناية الله سبحانه بالرد على هذه الصورة معنيين كبيرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealthy person imagines money can do anything, including warding off death, securing lasting life, and escaping God’s decree and judgment.
rows.anchor: كما يروح يحسب أن هذا المال إله قادر على كل شيء ؛ لا يعجز عن فعل شيء ! حتى دفع الموت وتخليد الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obsessive attachment to wealth leads him to count and savor it while scorning people’s dignity and mocking them through words and gestures.
rows.anchor: ينطلق في هوس بهذا المال يعده ويستلذ تعداده ؛ وتنطلق في كيانه نفخة فاجرة ، تدفعه إلى الاستهانة بأقدار الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam detests and forbids mockery and faultfinding; the sura’s severe warning suggests actual polytheists targeted the Messenger and believers, but Quṭb considers reports identifying particular people unreliable.
rows.anchor: وقد وردت روايات بتعيين بعض الشخصيات . ولكنها ليست وثيقة . فنكتفي نحن بما قررناه عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife scene proportionately reverses the crime: the rich scoffer who imagines wealth guarantees permanence is discarded and crushed in al-Ḥuṭama, the uniquely terrifying Fire attributed to God.
rows.anchor: المهمل المتردي في( الحطمة )التي تحطم كل ما يلقى إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire reaches his heart, source of mockery, arrogance, and pride, then confines him without aid or regard, tied to a pillar like an animal.
rows.anchor: على فؤاده الذي ينبعث منه الهمز واللمز ، وتكمن فيه السخرية والكبرياء والغرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quṭb notes emphatic sounds and rhetorical progression—threat, ambiguity, an awe-inspiring question, and explanation—to magnify the punishment and harmonize its imagery with the mocker’s acts.
rows.anchor: ثم سؤال الاستهوال . ثم الإجابة والبيان . . كلها من أساليب التوكيد والتضخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an directs the mission while recounting it, destroying enemies’ plots and strengthening believers; God’s answer both condemns ethical degradation and reassures the oppressed that He sees, hates, and punishes their abuse.
rows.anchor: إشعارهم بأن الله يرى ما يقع لهم ، ويكرهه ، ويعاقب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says akhladahu and khalladahu have the same meaning, then records four interpretations of the claim that wealth makes its possessor endure.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن أخلده وخلده بمعنى واحد ثم في التفسير وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan’s interpretation is that wealth lengthens the person’s hopes until, through heedlessness, he thinks it has made him immortal; the past tense pictures immortality as an already-secured guarantee against death.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : ما رأيت يقينا لا شك فيه أشبه بشك لا يقين فيه كالموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation is that he constructs durable buildings of brick and plaster as someone expecting to live on or to be remembered after death.
rows.anchor: يعمل الأعمال المحكمة كتشييد البنيان بالآجر والجص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view says he loves wealth so intensely that he imagines losing any of it would kill him and preserves it to stay alive; al-Rāzī considers this plausible for a miser.
rows.anchor: أحب المال حبا شديدا حتى اعتقد أنه إن انتقص مالي أموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth interpretation treats the statement as an allusion to righteous deeds, which preserve their doer through good remembrance in this world and enduring bliss in the next.
rows.anchor: أن هذا تعريض بالعمل الصالح وأنه هو الذي يخلد صاحبه في الدنيا بالذكر الجميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of kalla rebukes the delusion: wealth does not make one immortal, whereas knowledge and righteousness endure; ʿAlī is quoted saying wealth keepers die while scholars remain through time.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول علي عليه السلام : مات خزان المال وهم أحياء والعلماء باقون ما بقي الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second reading takes kalla to mean “indeed”; the lām in layunbadhanna answers an implied oath, conveying the force of an oath in kalla.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني معناه حقا : { لينبذن } واللام في : { لينبذن } جواب القسم المقدر
